$comment: AUTHORED. The only hand-edited file in design/tokens/. tokens.json, tokens.css, tokens.ts and contrast.md are all generated from this file by the build-tokens generator. COLOUR IS CARRIED unchanged from docs/05-marketing/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md Layer 1, which is LOCKED and founder-approved — not one hex here was adjusted, rounded or reinterpreted. TYPE IS DERIVED by arithmetic from the eleven numbers below, using the rules of agentvibe's docs/03-system-design/DESIGN-CAPABILITY.md 7.1 and measured against agentvibe's design/references/ corpus. CONTRAST IS COMPUTED on every run. THREE THINGS THE DESIGN LANGUAGE SPECIFIES ARE ABSENT BECAUSE THE SCHEMA CANNOT HOLD THEM, and each is named rather than approximated: the Instrument Serif display face (type.family takes only sans and mono), the asymmetric easing and 150-200ms durations (the generator has no motion group and would silently ignore one), and the structural numbers — radius, gutter, and the 65-character measure (no spacing group). Do not add a key for any of them here; a key nothing reads is worse than an absence somebody can see.

type.$comment: DERIVED, not authored. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md gives three faces and 'running text near 65 characters' and NO NUMBERS AT ALL, so the ramp below is a derivation and is stated as one. UI BAND: base 12, +2, five steps -> 12 14 16 18 20. That is vercel.com's measured marketing increment (+2, over 12 14 16) extended two steps, and every one of the five sizes appears in stripe.com's measured band; the range 12-20 is exactly the span 7.1 states for the UI band. It is deliberately NOT agentvibe's 11-15 control-plane band: 18 is the reading size for long-form prose, with 16 below it for dense passages and 20 above it for a lead. DISPLAY BAND: base 32, +16, three steps -> 32 48 64. +16 is the modal display increment in the corpus (linear.app +16 +16, stripe.com +16) and all three sizes are directly measured there (stripe.com 32 and 48, linear.app 48 and 64, vercel.com 64). THE JOIN is 20 -> 32, a ratio of 1.6 against a widest in-band step of 1.167 — a jump, not an interpolation. LEADING: peak 1.56 at 18px puts the top of 7.1's sourced 1.5-1.56 band exactly on the reading size, which is the right end of that band for a marketing site rather than a control plane. falloff 0.45 with exponent 1.0 gives 1.41 1.46 1.51 1.56 1.51 across the UI band; the exponent is 1 because nothing in the corpus argues for a curve shape and the linear falloff is the fit with one fewer invented constant. TRACKING: zeroAt 14 is 7.1's crossover. slope 0.0006 is set from the LARGE end, not the small one — this band spans 12 to 64px, 5.3x, and one linear function cannot give both a visible positive value at 12px and a sane negative one at 64px. 0.0006 yields -0.03em at the 64px hero and -0.02em at 48px, which is conventional for a high-contrast display serif; the consequence is that the positive tracking at 12px is +0.0012em, real in sign and invisible in effect. The uppercase-label letter-spacing DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md calls for is NOT this token: it is bound to case, not to size, and no size-derived function can express it.

family.$comment: TWO SLOTS, THREE FACES — the one thing in DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md's type section that this schema cannot hold. Instrument Serif (display: regular and italic only, no bold, so display emphasis is size and italic and never weight) has no slot: buildModel reads family.sans and family.mono and nothing else, so a serif key would reach no stylesheet and no TypeScript export. It is left out deliberately. CONSEQUENCE TO CARRY FORWARD: the display band below (32 48 64) is where Instrument Serif belongs, and under these tokens alone it would inherit --font-sans. The display face has to be bound at the component layer until the generator grows a third slot.
family.sans: 'Schibsted Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
family.mono: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

color.$comment: CARRIED, NOT DERIVED. Twelve values, verbatim from docs/05-marketing/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md Layer 1 — six roles across two chapters. Nothing here is generated and nothing here is a ramp. THE NAMES BIND THE CHAPTER FIRST, ON PURPOSE. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md's hardest rule is that the accent has two values that are NOT interchangeable, and a suffix form (accent-light / accent-dark) reads as a description of the VALUE rather than of the chapter — which inverts, because accent-dark would be the LIGHTER of the two hexes and picking it for a light ground is exactly the failure the rule exists to prevent. chapter-dark-accent cannot be misread that way. The system is otherwise neutral: photography owns colour, and the accent appears only on the primary CTA, at most twice per page.

contrastPairs.note: Body copy, light chapters. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AAA. No ratio is restated in any note here — the generated column is the only figure, because a carried figure is how the previous system's contrast table came to be wrong in both directions.

Body copy, dark chapters, on true black. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AAA. True black is load-bearing, not a style choice: the ground showing through between marks is the mechanism of every glyph and dot treatment.
Secondary text, light chapters. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AA. The lowest-contrast thing allowed to carry meaning in a light chapter.
Secondary text, dark chapters. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AA. The lowest-contrast thing allowed to carry meaning in a dark chapter.
Accent as text on the light ground — deep pine on warm bone. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AAA. The accent appears only on the primary CTA, at most twice per page.
Accent as text on the dark ground — pine tint on true black. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AAA. Same role as the row above, different chapter, different hex.

CTA fill, light chapters: warm bone knocked out of deep pine. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AAA. This is the pair above inverted, and it is listed separately because a fill and a text colour are different jobs even at the same ratio.
CTA fill, dark chapters: true black knocked out of pine tint. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md target: AAA.

REFUSAL, NOT A TARGET. The dark-chapter accent on the light ground. This row exists to FAIL and a pass here is the alarm: it would mean one of the two accents has been changed. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md states this as the hard rule: the two accents are not interchangeable, so ship them bound to the chapter and never as one. The schema has no field for an expected failure — this note is the only channel.

REFUSAL, NOT A TARGET. The light-chapter accent on the dark ground — the mirror of the row above, equally true and unwritten: DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md documents only the first direction. Encoding both is the point of a generated table. This row exists to FAIL and a pass here is the alarm.

SURFACE PAIR, deliberately below the text threshold. The hairline that exposes the column grid in light chapters. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md: hairlines are decorative structure, never interactive, never carrying information — so a text ratio is the wrong metric and a fail is the intended reading. Never a focus ring, never a control border.

SURFACE PAIR, deliberately below the text threshold. The hairline that exposes the column grid in dark chapters. Same rule as the row above: decorative structure only, and a fail is the intended reading.
